newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's central bank chief to address council.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's central bank chief to address council.

text.p: Algeria's Central Bank governor Abdelwahab Keramane will address Algeria's government-appointed Transitional National Council (CNT) on the country's monetary and financial situation, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Wednesday.
CNT speaker Abdelkader Bensalah on Wednesday opened the 100-day session of the body, a quasi-parliament appointed after the elected assembly was dissolved in January 1992.
The council is expected to vote a state budget law for 1997, a new privatisation law and election legislation.

"The significance of this session distinguishes it from previous ones because a set of subjects, mostly economic related ones, will be discussed," Bensalah told the opening session attended by Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia and his ministers.
Bensalah said Keramane would address the council to draw a picture of the country's financial health, but did not say when.
It will be the second time that an Algerian central bank chief has come out to an assembly to talk about the country's finances.
Keramane's predecessor Hadj Nacer Roustomi Abderrahmane was forced to appear before the parliament in 1991 over a disputed gold reserves swap.
